problem: The lead calls availability "the fifth member of the classic CIA triad". The CIA triad has exactly three members — confidentiality, integrity and availability — so availability cannot be a fifth member of it, and the sentence contradicts itself (four services plus a fifth, inside a set of three). Section 1 later states the triad correctly, so the lead leaves the student with two conflicting pictures.
fix: Rewrite as: "Cloud systems usually name four: confidentiality, integrity, authentication and non-repudiation. Many texts add availability, the A of the classic CIA triad, as a fifth security service."

where: Worked example 1, part (b) and the answer to part (c)
problem: Part (b) says a man-in-the-middle changes the amount from ₹10,000 to exactly ₹1,000, while part (c) says the same request was encrypted with a key held only by the app and the bank and concludes that confidentiality held. An attacker who cannot read the ciphertext cannot pick a new amount of their choosing; and if the attacker did read the amount, confidentiality failed. The answer to (c) therefore contradicts the scenario in (b) and teaches the wrong mental model (encryption stopping reading but allowing chosen edits).
fix: Separate the two cases. Make (b) plaintext tampering by a party that sees the request (for example a compromised component before the encryption step), with the MAC catching it. Then make (c) a clean hypothetical: "now suppose the same request is encrypted with a key shared only by the app and the bank — an eavesdropper on the wire learns nothing, so confidentiality holds, but encryption alone would still not detect a corrupted ciphertext; that is why the MAC (or an AEAD tag) is needed as well." Alternatively change (b) to a blind bit-flip that changes the amount to some unknown value, and drop the claim that it becomes ₹1,000.

problem: The caption says encryption appears only under confidentiality, but the table in Section 1 lists the AEAD tag as an integrity mechanism (AEAD is an encryption mode) and Section 2 says AES-GCM gives confidentiality and integrity together. The tree also shows integrity as "hash, MAC" only, and it drops availability even though the text calls availability a security service.
fix: Change the tree note for integrity to "hash, MAC, AEAD tag", add a fifth branch "Availability — replication, load balancing", and rewrite the caption to: "Encryption on its own sits only under confidentiality; the AEAD tag under integrity is part of an encryption mode that authenticates as it encrypts."
